title: Awake, unable to move, not alone

lines.text: You wake up. You can't move. And you feel like someone is in the room.
This is sleep paralysis. Somewhere between 8 and 50 percent of people have it at least once.
During dream sleep, your brain paralyses your body so you don't act out your dreams.
Sometimes, you wake up before that switch turns off.
Your mind is awake, but your body is still locked.
And dream imagery can leak into waking. Pressure on the chest, voices, a dark figure.
Cultures everywhere have named it. The Old Hag in Newfoundland. Kanashibari in Japan.
Episodes usually last a few minutes, and it's physically harmless.
Stress, sleep loss, and sleeping on your back can make it more likely.

sources.claim: Sleep paralysis affects 8% to 50% at least once; linked to REM characteristics persisting into waking; hallucinations include chest pressure and a dark figure; called Old Hag (Newfoundland), kanashibari (Japan); 1–6 minutes; physically harmless; triggers include stress, sleep deprivation, sleeping on the back
